ukratko: Two stories defined the day. Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang after a new affair, according to the WSJ. Google also launched the Gemini Decisions API, a new kind of model that doesn't write text but answers hundreds of yes/no questions in a couple hundred milliseconds. In its IPO filing, Anthropic revealed that its internal model moved Claude to AMD chips on its own in three days. There's also a practical note for Claude users: all paid plans get one free usage-limit reset.

vesti.naslov: Nvidia's board reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang
vesti.staSeDesilo: The New York Times reported that Huang had another affair, this time with Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. According to the Wall Street Journal, the board was due to decide as early as Wednesday whether to remove him after 33 years at the helm. The stock fell, and Republicans in Congress are demanding a closed-door briefing from him about his connection to a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Nvidia supplies nearly all the AI chips on the market, so chaos at the top affects pricing and compute availability for every AI company. The board has not made a final decision as far as the sources show, so follow official channels.

vesti.naslov: Gemini Decisions API: a model that only decides, up to 1,000 questions at once
vesti.staSeDesilo: Google released Gemini Decision 1 (`gemini-decision-1`). It's a "decision model": instead of generating text, it returns probabilities from 0 to 1 for closed questions (yes/no, pick from a list, rubric scoring). A single call takes text, images, audio, video or PDFs up to 256K tokens and up to 1,000 questions, and responds in 150 to 250 ms. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens, and output is free.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Small decisions inside an agent, such as routing, rule checks, tool selection and grading, no longer have to go through an expensive chat model. Amazon, for example, moved ticket tagging from Sonnet to a decision model that is 44 times cheaper. Simon Willison notes that a competing model, Jev, is still cheaper but only works with text.

vesti.naslov: Claude: free limit reset and MCP Apps in public preview
vesti.staSeDesilo: Anthropic says it fixed bugs that made Claude burn through more of your limits than it should. As compensation, Pro, Max, Ultra and Team users get one free full reset, usable until December 10. In addition, "MCP Apps", meaning tools and embedded sites that open inside Claude, entered public preview, and such apps also work in other clients that support the extension.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If Claude Code hit its limit too early for you this week, it wasn't you, and now you have one reset to make up for it. MCP Apps mean a UI you build once for a tool can work across multiple AI clients.

vesti.naslov: Anthropic: Mythos moved Claude to AMD chips in three days, "Autonomy 2" threshold reached
vesti.staSeDesilo: In an investor video, co-founder Tom Brown says Claude runs on four chip families (AWS Trainium, Google TPU, Nvidia and AMD). Moving to a new platform used to take dozens of engineers months, but the internal model Mythos got Claude running on AMD in three days, almost without humans, and wrote or ported nearly all the kernels (a kernel is the low-level code that runs on a chip). In its updated S-1, the IPO filing, Anthropic also says it believes the "Autonomy 2" threshold for accelerated AI development has been reached, though based on expectations of future models, not current ones.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If AI can port software from one chip to another this fast, Nvidia's CUDA is no longer an insurmountable advantage, which in the long run leads to cheaper inference for everyone. The threshold claim is also a signal that labs are seriously planning for AI that speeds up its own development.

vesti.naslov: "AI 2027" authors move their forecast again: a top-human-level AI researcher probably in 2027
vesti.staSeDesilo: The AI Futures Project, the group behind the well-known "AI 2027" scenario, now estimates that AI matching the best human AI researchers will probably arrive in 2027. Most of the authors had earlier pushed their dates into the 2030s. The main reason for the change is METR's estimate that Anthropic is progressing about twice as fast, mostly thanks to AI itself. Daniel Kokotajlo gives it a 50% chance by May 2027, while the other forecasters land between August and November.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This is a forecast, not a fact, but it comes from people the industry takes seriously, and it immediately spilled into the debate about slowing development. For developers, the practical takeaway is that coding tools will probably keep changing at this pace.

vesti.naslov: United Airlines bans AI agents from buying tickets
vesti.staSeDesilo: United doesn't allow personal AI assistants to book flights. It cites privacy, the risk of a purchase the user didn't intend, and federal rules, for example that a passenger must personally confirm there are no explosives in their luggage. Agents can still display United's flights, and the company says it hasn't seen many agent booking attempts so far.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This is the first big company to publicly close the door on agents buying on users' behalf, and it set off a large discussion on HN. If you're building an agent that buys or books, expect some sites to block it.

vesti.naslov: AWS releases an official local emulator of its services, written by a swarm of agents
vesti.staSeDesilo: Amazon published aws-emulator, an official local clone of AWS services for testing that doesn't need a paid account. It's written in Rust with the help of a large number of AI agents: 29,684 commits in the first three weeks. On macOS and Windows it currently requires Docker.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Tests against AWS can run locally and for free, with no cost and no real keys. The project is also one of the largest public examples of software written predominantly by AI.

vesti.naslov: Microsoft MAI-Transcribe-2: speech recognition for $0.10 per hour of audio
vesti.staSeDesilo: Microsoft released MAI-Transcribe-2, a speech-to-text model it claims is the fastest, most accurate and cheapest on the market. It can separate who is speaking (diarization), gives timestamps for every word, and offers several transcription styles. It costs $0.10 per hour of audio.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Transcribing meetings, podcasts and voice notes is becoming nearly free, which makes it a good foundation for small apps. The quality claims are Microsoft's own, and check the link for Serbian support.

vesti.naslov: OpenAI tops $10 billion in quarterly revenue, but still trails Anthropic
vesti.staSeDesilo: OpenAI had about $10 billion in revenue in the third quarter, nearly 50% more than in the second, but its operating loss grew to $10.9 billion. Anthropic had $17 billion in the same period. Ramp's index shows US corporate AI spending grew only 1.65% in October, and TSMC plans to invest $500 million each in OpenAI and Anthropic.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: The Decoder reports that this is pushing OpenAI into a price war for enterprise customers, which could bring discounts for API users. Slower spending growth is also a sign that the AI market is cooling.

vesti.naslov: Belgrade, November 18: how Tabby builds data infrastructure for AI agents
vesti.staSeDesilo: Startit is hosting a free talk at its AI Hub (Savska 5) from 6 PM by Maksim Zolotarev, head of the data platform at Tabby. The topic is why AI agents working over company data need more than data and an LLM, namely metadata and domain knowledge, along with the principles of "Docs/Infrastructure/Data as Code". The talk is in English and requires registration.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you're building an agent over a Supabase database, this is a practical first-hand topic, and it's free in Belgrade.

kratkeVesti.naslov: Helsing unveiled Clarity, a platform where agents turn sensor data into target proposals for weapons systems, with a promise that a human signs off on every decision.
DeepL Voice is getting a new model that carries the speaker's tone, emotion, accent and pace across in live translation.
The UK higher-education regulator is threatening universities with sanctions unless they bring back exams that AI can't do for students.
According to a ChinaTalk investigation, US data firms such as Mercor and Surge AI have sold Chinese labs training environments worth around half a billion dollars.
The indie scene is rocked by an AI debate after the developers of Big Walk admitted using AI to fix a bug, and 19 IGF award juries refuse to vote for games with generative AI.
Parents claim their 13-year-old daughter spent weeks planning suicide through Gemini on a school Chromebook, and that school monitoring didn't notice.
Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA changes affect individual cell types; it's available via API for non-commercial research.
Google Labs is testing Tabletop, shared group spaces where AI builds polls, itineraries and expense splitters from a description; for now US-only, via a waitlist.
Mercor, a company that pays experts to create AI training data, raised $750 million at a $20 billion valuation and $3 billion in annual run-rate revenue.
OpenAI disclosed that on July 19, during a cyber test, five agents used leftover credentials to access its research infrastructure, including private grading code.
OpenAI acquired Odessia, a young AI trip-planning startup, and its founder is joining OpenAI to work on travel.
UK AI chip maker Fractile raised $720 million.
CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay upfront and offering shorter contracts, which could push compute prices up.
MBZUAI released PAN 2 under the Apache 2.0 license, an open 29-billion-parameter "world model" that simulates the outcome of a scene and described action as video.
Fish Audio released Live 3, a voice model that listens while it speaks, so the other person can interrupt it or throw in an "uh-huh" without breaking the conversation.
Nvidia released GR00T 2 as an open robot model, along with 100,000 hours of training data, a simulator and hardware designs.
Cursor reworked Projects so that agents from different team members share plans and warn each other about conflicts.
China is introducing a separate approval process for phones, tablets and wearables with pre-installed AI agents.
More than a hundred activists stormed the construction site of Microsoft's AI data center in Amsterdam, and protests against data centers took place in 16 countries.
Version 0.37.2 of Willison's llm tool fixes two bugs that could accidentally send an OpenAI key to a different provider, so it's worth updating.

istrazivanje.objasnjenje: Agents that remember "lessons" from earlier tasks often start making mistakes because of bad or outdated memories. WikiTrace stores, alongside each lesson, the workflow it came from and the reasoning behind it, so the agent checks whether it still holds before applying it and corrects it if needed.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: It transfers easily to CLAUDE.md and similar rules files: attach a link to the commit or issue it came from to each rule. On agentic benchmarks, this reduced the performance degradation caused by bad memory.

istrazivanje.naslov: Infrathon: agents optimize real AI infrastructure for 24 hours
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: A new benchmark gives agents long AI-infrastructure optimization tasks with a 24-hour budget per attempt: six models, 150 attempts, over 10,000 GPU-hours. The model leaderboard changes depending on test length, and 135 of 150 attempts kept making progress in the second half of the time. Claude Opus 5.5 beat the human-built solution on one task.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: It shows that short tests underestimate agents, and it lists the most common pitfalls: breaking task rules, unreliable tests and declaring victory too early. These are the same things to watch for when you give Claude Code long tasks.

istrazivanje.naslov: MMDM: a big benchmark for decision models
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: A benchmark with 5,448 questions across 16 categories measures how well models make structured decisions in a single pass, without writing out their reasoning: which tool to choose, tracking agent state, rubric grading. There are 2 to 1,024 options to choose from, and inputs run past 64,000 tokens. 28 models were tested.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: It arrives the same day as Google's Decisions API, so it's useful for checking how far you can trust such models before handing them routing in your app.

ideje.problem: Listings on KupujemProdajem and similar sites have blurry photos, the wrong category, or a description that doesn't match the picture, so they sell slowly.
ideje.zaKoga: People selling used items in Serbia and small shops that post many listings
ideje.ulogaAi: Gemini Decision 1 gets an image and text in a single call and answers about ten yes/no questions (is the photo sharp, is the whole item visible, does the description match the image, is the condition mentioned). The app turns that into a fix-it list.
prviKoraci: Create an API key in Google AI Studio and try 10 questions on a few of your own photos in the playground
Angular page: image upload, a description field and a "Check" button
Supabase Edge Function that calls gemini-decision-1 and returns probabilities; show anything below 0.5 as a suggested fix
Finally, add one call to a cheap text model that suggests a better title

ideje.problem: At tenant assemblies, building councils or associations, nobody keeps minutes, so afterward no one knows who said what and what was agreed.
ideje.zaKoga: Chairs of tenant assemblies, small associations and local clubs
ideje.ulogaAi: MAI-Transcribe-2 turns the recording into text and separates speakers, and Claude turns that into minutes with decisions, assignments and deadlines in Serbian.
prviKoraci: Check on Microsoft's model page whether, and how well, it supports Serbian
SwiftUI app that records via AVAudioRecorder and uploads the file to Supabase Storage
Edge Function: transcription with diarization, then Claude Sonnet with a prompt for the minutes format
PDF export and a shareable link for the building's Viber group

ideje.problem: For a slava, a birthday or a barbecue, planning runs through a chaotic Viber group: who brings what, who has paid, how much each person owes.
ideje.zaKoga: Groups of friends and families in Serbia who organize get-togethers
ideje.ulogaAi: From a single sentence ("barbecue for 12 people on Saturday, we're collecting 1,500 dinars each") the AI builds an item list, a date poll and an expense table, and the space is shared via a link with no sign-up.
prviKoraci: Supabase tables: event, items, participants and payments, with a public link via a random token
Angular page with Supabase Realtime so everyone sees changes live
Edge Function with Claude Haiku that builds the initial item list as JSON from the description
A "Share on Viber" button with a link to the event
ideje.inspiracija: Google Tabletop, which is only available in the US and only via a waitlist

ideje.problem: Universities are going back to oral and traditional exams because of AI, and students have no one to practice answering aloud with.
ideje.zaKoga: University and high-school students preparing for an oral exam or entrance test
ideje.ulogaAi: From uploaded study notes, the AI asks questions by voice, listens to the answer, grades it against a rubric and tells you what was missed.
prviKoraci: SwiftUI app: import a PDF of notes and split it into topics
Claude generates questions and a grading rubric for each topic
Record and transcribe the answer (Apple Speech or a transcription API), then grade it against the rubric
Track weak topics in Supabase and ask about them first the next day
ideje.inspiracija: The UK regulator demanding AI-proof exams

ideje.problem: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files fill up over time with rules nobody remembers the reason for, so the agent follows outdated instructions.
ideje.zaKoga: Developers working with Claude Code and other coding agents
ideje.ulogaAi: A CLI tool adds to each rule in CLAUDE.md a link to the commit or PR it came from, and Claude periodically checks whether the rule is still accurate against the current code.
prviKoraci: Node CLI that parses CLAUDE.md and finds the last linked commit for each rule (git log -S)
Format: rule + <!-- source: hash --> comment
An `audit` command sends the rule and the relevant diff to Claude and asks "does this still hold?"
Build it as a Claude Code plugin/skill, modeled on addyosmani/agent-skills
ideje.inspiracija: The WikiTrace paper (memory with evidence) and agent-skills from GitHub Trending

cene: Several models got cheaper today: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (input from $0.051 to $0.022, output from $0.567 to $0.4), gpt-oss-20b ($0.018/$0.09, previously $0.03/$0.13), Qwen3.5-9B ($0.118/$0.174, previously $0.17/$0.25) and MiniMax M2.5 ($0.27/$1.08, previously $0.3/$1.2). GPT-5.6 Sol (from $4/$20 to $4.4/$22, which is 120% more than 30 days ago) and GLM 5.1 (from $1.33/$4.18 to $1.4/$4.4) got more expensive. The cheapest input in the cheap-and-fast class is now DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at $0.022, the cheapest output is GLM 5.3 Flash at $0.0784, and the new Claude Fable 5.2 costs $8/$40, while Fable 5.1 is $10/$50.

teme.oCemuSePrica: After the admission of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, reports of a second affair with a subordinate executive have surfaced, and the WSJ says the board is considering removing him. The debate is about whether national security is at risk and how Nvidia was getting licenses to sell chips to Chinese shell companies in the first place.
teme.glasovi: Journalists and analysts on X (@jingyanghk, @robertwiblin) add details about the chips that ended up in China and how the investigation unfolded. On Mastodon, mockery and "AI bubble" talk dominate. Nvidia says no secrets were leaked.

teme.naslov: Fable 5.2 vs. Gemini 4 Carbon: which is better per dollar
teme.oCemuSePrica: The first independent tests are arriving in bulk. Fable 5.2 is often the best, but it uses several times more tokens, so it costs much more per task: according to SemiAnalysis, 7.5 times more than Carbon. Carbon is cheaper, but testers report hallucination and overconfidence.
teme.glasovi: SemiAnalysis and Artificial Analysis are publishing cost-per-task calculations. Theo and @leo_linsky report "dumb mistakes" from Fable, and that mid-task it asked for a decision from a human who wasn't there. @krishnanrohit and @kimmonismus write about Carbon's weaknesses, and Google's Logan Kilpatrick objects that Gemini wasn't tested in its own environment in one comparison.

teme.naslov: United bans agents: can websites block your AI assistant?
teme.oCemuSePrica: United's decision to bar AI agents from buying tickets raised the question of who is responsible when an agent buys the wrong thing, and whether companies are just protecting their own sales channels.
teme.glasovi: On Hacker News (422 points, over 400 comments), some praise the caution given fraud and wrong purchases, while others argue it's the same as blocking browser extensions and that the law will eventually have to settle it.

teme.naslov: "AI 2027" authors: a superhuman AI researcher possibly as soon as next year
teme.oCemuSePrica: The AI Futures Project's new forecast and Kokotajlo's statement that he is "scared, sad and angry" reignited the debate about pausing development. Vals AI's trend shows a similar date, August 2027.
teme.glasovi: @DKokotajlo is driving the conversation and wants a pause to be a priority. Vals AI and some researchers give even more aggressive estimates, while skeptics remind everyone that this is still a forecasting model, not a measured fact.

teme.naslov: "My AI agents found an unmapped Maya site?"
teme.oCemuSePrica: A personal blog post about agents that analyzed public data and pointed to a possible undiscovered Maya site became the most popular AI post of the day on HN. The question mark in the title matters: the finding hasn't been confirmed in the field.
teme.glasovi: HN commenters (937 points) split between those thrilled by what one person can do with agents and archaeologists and skeptics who demand verification before any conclusions.
